# CANDIDATE: BEARISH_REJECTION_VOL_FILTER

**Filed:** 2026-07-21  
**Filer:** chef-nemotron (free-tier autonomous R&D)  
**Type:** filter_change  
**Status:** DRAFT (NEEDS-RATIFICATION per Rule 9)

## Hypothesis

The BEARISH_REJECTION_RIDE_THE_RIBBON setup captures only ~50% of the available winner-day P&L (edge_capture=780 vs max 1542), with particular underperformance on 4/29 and 5/01. Adding a volatility filter that requires elevated ATR aims to increase capture of large, momentum-driven moves like 5/04 while avoiding choppy conditions that lead to premature exits or missed entries.

## Mechanism

Enter BEARISH_REJECTION_RIDE_THE_RIBBON only when the 5-minute ATR(20) > 1.5 × median(ATR(20)) over the prior 20 bars. This condition is evaluated at the trigger bar. All other entry/exit logic remains unchanged: chart-stop primary invalidation, chandelier profit-lock arms at +5%, trails 0.15, TP1 at +50% (2/3 qty), runner exits on re-entry into EMA ribbon or TP2, time stop 15:50 ET.

## OP-20 disclosures

1. **Account-size assumption:** qty=28 requires $25K+; $1K paper ~= 14% headline  
2. **Sample bias:** Stage-1 backtest will use 16 months of SPY 5m data (2025-01-02 to 2026-06-18) with real OPRA fills; risk of overfit to volatility regimes; walk-forward held-out window will mitigate.  
3. **Out-of-sample:** NEEDS-OOS (will run walk-forward after Stage-1)  
4. **Real-fills:** NEEDS-REAL-FILLS (will validate top-3 J days via realistic simulator)  
5. **Failure modes:** Worst day: volatility filter fails to trigger on a large move (e.g., 5/04-like day with atypical ATR); max drawdown scenario: filter triggers excessively in chop, increasing losers; blow-up scenario: filter misfires during volatility spike causing multiple consecutive losses.  
6. **Concentration:** If top-5 days = X% of P&L, state X (unknown -- requires Stage-1 backtest)
